public_rationale: The evidence documents both parts of the claim. FActScore found substantial unsupported factual content in generated biographies. A separate planning study found frequent failures by GPT-4 on tasks with mechanically checkable solutions. This supports the ordinary reading that factual and reasoning outputs still needed verification. The planning study also found improvements and useful roles for external assistance; those findings do not establish that the underlying reliability problems had been solved.
limitations: The results concern specific models, tasks, and prompts rather than every possible use.
The studies were reported in May; they are not a direct test of every model update available on September 21.
The sources do not identify exact dates for every experimental run.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that contemporary general-purpose LLMs still produce unsupported factual assertions and material reasoning errors, so unchecked answers are not dependable.
This does not assert that every answer is wrong or that no bounded application can use an LLM reliably.
Factuality and reasoning require separate evidence; neither is inferred solely from the other.
No measurement period is specified. I use the six-month retrospective named in the title, ending on publication, as the reporting window for the continuing state.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations establish dependable factual accuracy and reasoning across the claimed general-purpose scope, with the alleged recurring failures absent.
